headline: Nifty at a nine-month high on foreign buying; Nvidia turmoil clouds the open

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning, and welcome to your Market Brief for Thursday, the twelfth of November.

Three things matter most today. First, foreign money is pouring back into Indian shares, and it lifted the Nifty to its highest close in nine months yesterday. Second, Bajaj Finance has launched a share sale of up to 11,700 crore rupees, one of the biggest of the year. And third, overnight, reports that Nvidia's board may remove its chief executive Jensen Huang sent the chipmaker's shares sharply lower after hours, which could set the tone for technology stocks across Asia this morning.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Now to how markets closed on Wednesday. The Nifty rose 0.84 percent to 25,255, and the Sensex gained 0.95 percent, or about 770 points, to 81,879. That is the highest close for both since the twenty-sixth of February. At one point in the day the Nifty touched about 25,600 before giving back some of the gain.

Autos, consumer goods and financials led the way. Banks were the real story. The Bank Nifty has rallied around 4 percent in two days and is now close to its record high of 61,765, set in February. Bank of Baroda and Punjab National Bank rose about 5 percent each, and Punjab National Bank hit a fifty-two-week high. Ashoka Buildcon jumped 15 percent on an 866 crore rupee expressway contract, and fertiliser makers FACT, Coromandel and GSFC gained up to 9 percent after the Cabinet cleared the winter-crop subsidy.

The fuel is foreign money. Foreign institutional investors bought about 12,560 crore rupees of Indian shares on Wednesday alone, according to provisional data. For November so far, estimates of their buying range from around six and a half to seven and a half billion dollars, already their biggest monthly purchase since September 2024. Brokerages are turning more positive too. Citi has raised its Nifty target to 28,000, HSBC has upgraded Indian shares to overweight, and Bernstein has lifted its target to 26,100.

Levels to watch, according to analysts: support around 25,000, then 24,800. Resistance is the 25,400 to 25,500 zone, and a clear move above that could open the way to 25,900 or 26,000. For the Bank Nifty, Wednesday's high of 61,394 is the hurdle. GIFT Nifty points to a flat to muted start this morning.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
On to deals. Bajaj Finance has launched a qualified institutions placement to raise up to 11,700 crore rupees. The indicative price is 1,025 rupees a share, about a 5 percent discount to Wednesday's close, and the money will go towards repaying borrowings and general corporate needs.

In other deal news, Canada's Fairfax Financial is likely to sell its stake of nearly 11 percent in IIFL Finance, worth around 3,000 crore rupees, according to sources quoted by the Economic Times. The aim is to raise money for a big stake in IDBI Bank. Dixon Technologies has sold half its holding in Aditya Infotech, the parent of CP Plus, for 582 crore rupees, with two mutual fund schemes as buyers.

Index changes matter this week too. In its November review, MSCI has added LIC, Adani Green, Meesho and Coforge to its emerging markets index, and dropped PI Industries. The changes take effect on the thirtieth of November. Nuvama's research team expects Coforge to see the biggest inflows, around 630 million dollars, followed by LIC at about 468 million dollars.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now the results roundup, and it was a mixed bag.

Among manufacturers, costs are biting. MRF's revenue rose almost 18 percent to 8,524 crore rupees, but total expenses grew more than 22 percent, squeezing margins and profit because of higher raw material costs. Citi still keeps its outperform rating, and Centrum expects margins to recover. Whirlpool of India's profit fell 40 percent to about 25 crore rupees, which the company linked to inflation, crude oil prices and a weaker rupee. Avanti Feeds' profit fell 55 percent to about 69 crore rupees, and the stock slipped 6 percent.

On the brighter side, Cupid's quarterly profit more than doubled to around 56 crore rupees, and it raised its revenue guidance for this financial year to at least 880 crore rupees. Among jewellers, Kalyan Jewellers' profit rose 64 percent and PC Jeweller's 58 percent. EAAA India Alternatives posted a 27 percent rise in profit to 88 crore rupees and declared an interim dividend of 7 rupees a share.

Rentomojo, which listed in September, reported profit of about 18 crore rupees, up 125 percent from the previous quarter on revenue up 53 percent from a year ago, though Business Standard notes that profit is lower than a year earlier. The stock still jumped 10 percent.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy, starting with tax. Net direct tax collections from the first of April to the tenth of November rose 11.8 percent to 14.42 lakh crore rupees. Gross collections were up 14 percent at 17.5 lakh crore rupees. Corporate tax led the way, up nearly 18 percent to 6.32 lakh crore rupees, while non-corporate taxes, which include individuals, grew a slower 5.3 percent to 7.56 lakh crore rupees. Refunds jumped about 26 percent. Net collections are now at 53.5 percent of the full-year budget target.

On growth, Moody's has raised its forecast for this financial year to 7 percent, from 6.5 percent, citing strong consumption and resilience to the energy shock. It did flag risks: inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank's 2 to 6 percent range, a weak monsoon and El Nino. SBI Research expects September-quarter growth of 7.8 percent, above the Reserve Bank's estimate of 7.2 percent.

The rupee touched a six-month high of 93.69 to the dollar on Wednesday, helped by foreign inflows, but closed slightly weaker at 93.93 as state-run banks bought dollars, ending a six-day winning streak.

The Union Cabinet had a busy day. It approved a fertiliser subsidy of 62,370 crore rupees for the winter crop season, up 64 percent, and kept the price of DAP fertiliser at 1,350 rupees a bag. It extended the Stand-Up India loan scheme to 2031 with a 4,111 crore rupee guarantee corpus, set aside 5,000 crore rupees for a MUDRA credit guarantee fund, and cleared a 2,390 crore rupee extension of the Noida Metro Aqua Line.

On trade, the government has banned exports of unsorted battery waste, including lithium-ion black mass, with immediate effect. Customs has held Scotch shipments of Pernod and Diageo, arguing bulk concentrates don't qualify for the reduced 75 percent duty under the trade pact and should pay 150 percent.

One for the budget wish list: industry body PHDCCI wants long-term capital gains tax on shares scrapped and the short-term rate cut to 10 percent in the coming Union Budget.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, Wall Street had a strong session. The Dow rose about half a percent, the S&P 500 1.3 percent and the Nasdaq 1.6 percent, as the artificial intelligence trade bounced back. CoreWeave surged 25 percent on strong results and guidance, and Micron jumped 12 percent.

But the mood turned after the bell. Reports said Nvidia's board may oust chief executive Jensen Huang, and the stock fell around 7 to 8 percent in after-hours trade, pulling Nasdaq futures lower. Nvidia was already down 29 percent from its October high, Baird has cut its price target by 60 percent, and the company reports results on the seventeenth of November. Asian markets are mixed this morning.

Oil is easing. Brent crude is around 92 dollars a barrel, down about 1 percent, and well below its peak of 118 dollars on the thirtieth of October. Talks between the United States and Iran remain stuck, and Israel is reported to be preparing for a possible strike, so the risk hasn't gone away.

The dollar is at its strongest since April 2025, as traders raise bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money. Mutual fund investors slowed down in October. Net inflows into equity funds fell 14 percent to about 33,000 crore rupees, from 38,306 crore rupees in September, though it was the sixtieth straight month of inflows. Monthly SIP contributions dipped slightly to 32,160 crore rupees. Money moved away from small and midcap funds and towards large-cap funds.

For home loan borrowers, HDFC Bank has raised its lending rate benchmark by 5 to 15 basis points across all tenures, effective the seventh of November, so floating-rate loans linked to it will cost a little more.

Two rulings worth knowing. The Supreme Court has clarified that the 500-gram gold limit for married women does not by itself explain where the jewellery came from in disproportionate-assets cases, so keep your purchase records. And a consumer commission ruled for a pensioner's family after Tata AIG denied a 30 lakh rupee death claim over alleged alcohol use, saying the insurer lacked reliable evidence.

Good news for non-resident Indians: from the third of December, Sebi will let them complete investment KYC from abroad without being physically present in India.

That's the brief. Today, watch how Indian tech stocks react to the Nvidia news at the open, whether the Nifty can clear the 25,400 to 25,500 zone, how the Bajaj Finance share sale is received, and whether foreign buying keeps going. Have a good day.
